test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the primary objective of the 'Sahkar' taxi service, launched by the Indian government in March 2025?

options.text: To empower drivers through a cooperative, profit-sharing model
To establish a government-owned ride-hailing monopoly
To provide free taxi services to senior citizens
To replace all existing private taxi services in India

solution:
The correct answer is __**To empower drivers through a cooperative, profit-sharing model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Sahkar' taxi service was launched by the Indian government in March 2025 to **empower drivers through a cooperative model**, ensuring equitable profit-sharing.
 
• It aims to provide a sustainable livelihood for drivers by eliminating intermediary exploitation and promoting transparency in the industry.
 
• The service functions as a driver-owned cooperative, where profits are distributed among the members, fostering social and financial inclusion.
 
• This initiative aligns with the government's agenda of promoting cooperative enterprises as a way to boost employment and self-reliance.
 
• The Sahkar taxi service is expected to encourage fair practices and improve working conditions for drivers in India, especially in urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cooperative Model:**

 
 
• A cooperative is a member-owned organization that operates for the benefit of its members rather than external shareholders.
 
• It is based on principles of voluntary participation, democratic governance, and equitable profit-sharing.
 
• Cooperatives often focus on improving livelihoods and promoting social equity.
 
 
 
• **Indian Government Initiatives in Cooperative Sector:**
 
 
• The government has been actively promoting cooperatives through schemes like the **National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC)**.
 
• It has introduced legislative reforms to strengthen cooperative societies and improve their governance.
 
 
 
• **Employment Generation through Cooperatives:**
 
 
• Cooperative enterprises are known to create sustainable employment opportunities by reducing dependency on external funding.
 
• They empower individuals by offering them a stake in the organization and its profits.
 
 
 
• **Urban Mobility Challenges:**
 
 
• India's urban areas face significant challenges in mobility due to increasing population and traffic congestion.
 
• Initiatives like the 'Sahkar' taxi service aim to address these challenges while ensuring fair practices for drivers.
